applies_to: Trane Voyager 3 packaged rooftop air conditioners with the Symbio 700 controller.
summary: Symbio 700 is the factory controller on Voyager 3 rooftops. It speaks BACnet IP, BACnet MS/TP or BACnet over Zigbee (Air-Fi), and the same guide maps every object to Modbus. Objects use 5-digit instances (AI-10101, AV-11403...). Most writable objects are BAS or Setpoint values that feed Trane's arbitration logic, and the BAS sensor values carry a 900 s heartbeat.
notes: Only the points that match the unit's factory configuration show up; the guide lists every possible point.
Name suffixes carry meaning: Status/Local/Active/Input are read-only, BAS/Command/Request/Setpoint value objects are the ones a BAS writes, and Arbitrator objects show which source is winning.

Access 'C' marks writable objects whose arbitration pattern is setpoint with a priority array, plus AV 10127, AV 10159 and AV 10160, which the appendix calls commandable; other writable objects are 'W'.

Several objects are printed more than once with different descriptions or state lists for different unit configurations (PI gain/reset AVs, AI 11142-11143, BI 11231, BV 11100, MV 11110 Service Test State Request, MV 11128). Each is listed once here.
Eight objects whose rows ran together in the table (AI 10185, AI 10187, AV 11159, AV 11160, AV 11217, AV 11218, BV 11127, BV 11128) were checked against the page text.
The same guide gives Modbus RTU/TCP registers for every object; only the BACnet side is listed here.

integration.summary: Leave MV 11100 Arbitration Method Request at 'Enable External/BAS Control'. Then schedule the unit with MV 10106 Occupancy Request and send setpoints to the setpoint BAS points at a priority above 14. If the BMS supplies sensor values such as space temperature, rewrite the '... BAS' points within their 900 s heartbeat.

integration.enable: MV 11100 Arbitration Method Request picks the control type. 'Enable External/BAS Control' is the default: the controller weighs BAS, Air-Fi and wired sources. 'Standalone Control' ignores all BAS input and is meant for troubleshooting. BV 11113 Unit Stop Command (Auto/Stop) stops the unit from the BMS.
integration.heartbeat: The sensor BAS points (AV 10113 Outdoor Air Temperature BAS, AV 10114 Space Temperature BAS, AV 10116-10119, AV 11103 Return Air Humidity BAS, AV 11119 Return Air Temperature BAS) have a 900 s heartbeat in the tables, so the BMS must keep rewriting them. The setpoint and command points have no heartbeat.
integration.remote_sensors: Write the value to the matching '... BAS' AV (e.g. AV 10114 Space Temperature BAS, AV 10113 Outdoor Air Temperature BAS) and keep refreshing it; the '... Arbitrator' object shows which source wins and the '... Active' object reports the value in use. Space setpoints go to AV 10127 (single setpoint) or AV 10159/10160 (dual setpoint). BV 10113 Occupancy Input BAS is the communicated occupancy input.
setup: The rotary address (001-127) sets the BACnet MS/TP MAC and the default Device ID; changing it takes effect without a power cycle.
A software Device ID (1-4194302) can be set in the Symbio Service and Installation mobile app (Bluetooth) or on the onboard display.
MS/TP default baud is 76,800 bps; MS/TP wiring lands on connector J17. BACnet IP uses the Ethernet port.
For BACnet IP set the IP address first, then the protocol, Device ID and UDP port; tick BBMD only if this is the only BACnet IP device on the subnet.
Communicated units can be switched between IP and SI in the mobile app or onboard display.
gotchas: Wired setpoints write at priority 15 and Air-Fi at 14, so the BMS must write setpoint BAS points at a priority above 14 or the value is ignored.
Setpoints changed from the onboard display or mobile app go to the relinquish default, not the priority array.
Arbitrator objects are for reading only, even though the table marks them writable.
'Command' points may be persisted once written, so don't write them cyclically.
Air-Fi installs are integrated through a Tracer SC+ system controller, not directly.
